featured_reviews.name: Mandar Keny
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shivraj Dhaba Karad, located in Prabhadevi, Mumbai, offers a taste of authentic highway-style pure vegetarian cooking right in the city. It’s the perfect place for anyone craving hearty North Indian and Maharashtrian dhaba food.
The atmosphere is simple and purely functional—don't expect fancy decor or quiet dining. It’s often busy and buzzing, giving it a genuine roadside feel which enhances the experience. Service is generally quick and efficient, even during busy weekend hours.
The menu is quite limited, but the real stars are the spicy Maharashtrian curries and rich preparations. Their fresh Bhakri and Tandoori Rotis are essential for scooping up the flavorful gravies. If you like bold, rustic flavors, definitely try the signature Akkha Masura which is the star . The portions are enough for 2 people , which means you get excellent value for your money.
Overall, this is a wonderful spot for a satisfying meal that feels truly authentic and homemade. It’s a great choice for families and friends looking for delicious, spicy comfort food at reasonable prices. Shivraj Dhaba Karad is highly recommended for a genuine dhaba experience without leaving Mumbai.

We visited Nude Food Café as a group of five and, unfortunately, the experience didn’t go as well as we hoped. Although we were told the wait would be around 20 minutes, we ended up waiting 1.5 hours for a table, while others seemed to be seated much faster. The staff and owners were polite, but the communication about wait times needs improvement, and there were no proper waiting arrangements.

On the positive side, the café has a great eco-friendly concept with a zero-waste food policy, which I really appreciate. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, even though the space feels a bit small and crowded.

The coffee was excellent, the chicken pie was tasty (could’ve used a spicy note), and the pasta dishes were nice, though one was slightly undercooked and could have used more spice. Portions felt a bit small for the price.

Overall, while the café’s concept and ambience are lovely, the extremely slow service and long wait time took away from the experience. Expanding the seating area or managing reservations more clearly would help a lot.

The paneer items, in particular, are perfectly cooked and bursting with flavor, while the dosa varieties come with authentic sambhar and chutneys that are simply irresistible.

What sets this restaurant apart is its impeccable balance of quality and quantity. The food is not only delicious but also served generously, ensuring great value for money. The ambiance is clean and welcoming, making it a comfortable place for families and groups.

Whether you’re looking for a hearty meal or a quick bite, Siddhivinayak Veg Restaurant delivers on all fronts. The staff is courteous, service is prompt, and the flavors are truly satisfying.

Pro Tip: Visit during non-peak hours to avoid waiting times, especially during busy temple days. Don’t miss their signature paneer dishes and chole bhature – they’re worth every bite!

✅ Highly Recommended for all devotees and food enthusiasts visiting Siddhivinayak Temple.

Except for the "ok-ok" dishes, everything else was soo darn yum! Service by #Kunal was very friendly and kind. What a fantastic meal!!

Dont miss out on their Sol Kadi, their Crab Lollipop and the Kharwas. Baki jo marzi order karo. 😊

featured_reviews.name: Prasad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Chaitanya for the second time, and it’s still one of the best places for authentic Konkan Malvani food in Dadar, Mumbai. Truly one of the rare restaurants that serves genuinely authentic seafood
Chaitanya easily ranks at the top!
The place is always crowded, so be prepared to wait outside for at least 20–40 minutes. The seating area is small, but the food makes it completely worth the wait. Prices depend on the current fish rates.
We tried the special prawns thali, which comes with double portions of prawns fry absolutely delicious. Also had the surmai thali with two fried pieces, and the taste was awesome. The bhakri was soft and fresh.
The best part was the unlimited solkadi, along with tasty crab lollipop. Service was quick too—food arrived within 5–10 minutes. Highly recommended for seafood lovers!

You must visit to this place and do try the amazing food of Indian west costline. This place will not disappoint you at all..

featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flavours Of China in Prabhadevi is a solid go-to spot for Indo-Chinese and Thai cuisine, especially if you’re looking for tasty food at reasonable pricing in the South Mumbai area.

🍽️ Food:
The food is definitely the highlight here. Their menu offers a wide variety—from classic Chinese gravies and noodles to Thai curries and rice. Dishes like burnt garlic rice, Manchurian, and Thai curries stand out for their bold flavours and generous portions. The taste is consistent, slightly on the Indianised side (which most people prefer), and perfect for comfort dining. Many customers also appreciate the freshness and customizable options available.

🥢 Portion Size & Value:
Portions are quite generous, making it ideal for sharing. Pricing is pocket-friendly for the quality and quantity offered, making it a great value-for-money option in the area.

🏠 Ambience:
The ambience is simple and casual—not a fine dining place, but clean and comfortable for a quick meal with friends or family. Seating space is slightly limited, so it can feel a bit cramped during peak hours.

🧑‍🍳 Service:
Service is generally quick, especially for takeaway and delivery orders. However, during busy hours, there can be slight delays and service could be more attentive.

📍 Location:
Conveniently located in Prabhadevi near Century Bazaar, it’s easily accessible and a popular neighbourhood dining spot.

⸻

✅ Pros:

* Delicious Indo-Chinese flavours
* Generous portion sizes
* Good value for money
* Wide menu variety (Chinese + Thai)

Modakam Restaurant ,Near Siddhivinayak Temple
Modakam restaurant, located just beside Siddhivinayak Mandir, is a great place to visit after darshan. I honestly didn’t expect such authentic and fresh food.
They serve freshly made Ukdiche Modak, which is a must-try. The restaurant offers a good variety of Maharashtrian and North Indian dishes.

The service was good and staff were polite. However, you may have to wait around 15–20 minutes for seating, especially during peak hours, but it’s definitely worth the wait.
Overall, it’s a must-visit place near Siddhivinayak Temple if you want to enjoy good food after darshan.

We had their Punjabi Thali, happy to see that because it was as same as displayed on the hotel walls as a covershot. Because very few restaurants serves food as displayed on the menu. The thali looked beautiful and delicious as well, looking at my thali the new customers who sat beside me also enquired me with which is the dish and also ordered the same. Also we tried their modam which was piping hot drizzled with ghee. Even if the place is compact and small but it's clean and hygiene maintained is very well, service is fast and well managed to maintain the flow of crowd due to small place even with the place constraint the menu range is wide and long. featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

featured_reviews.review_text: The food was better than average, the ambience was good, and the service was quick. featured_reviews.name: Sagar Jondhale
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently dined here and had a mixed experience. I tried the Veg Kolhapuri with garlic butter naan, which was delicious, though I found the naan size smaller than what I’m used to from other restaurants. The Jeera Rice was also well-prepared and tasty, meeting my expectations.

However, the jalapeno rolls were disappointing. They were overly crispy and didn’t have any noticeable jalapeno flavor, making them not worth it. Dessert was a highlight, though – the warm Gulab Jamun was just perfect!

Service could definitely use some improvement. Although the restaurant wasn’t crowded as it was an off-peak time, it took quite a while for dishes to arrive. The jalapeno rolls came 20 minutes after ordering, almost at the end of my main course, and the Jeera Rice took another 10-15 minutes to be served.

Overall, it was an okay experience. Some dishes were delightful, but the slow service and a few underwhelming items left room for improvement.

Well, the place is very well maintained with a good staff. Although it is a small place it is well maintained and kept clean. I enjoyed my dining experience here.

featured_reviews.name: Kaustubh Havanur
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best places for pure vegetarian food. This place is easily accessible as it is located right on the main road near Sena Bhavan. You can get down at Dadar Metro Station, and as soon as you come onto the main road, the restaurant is right beside it.

Whenever you visit, you will almost always find a rush here. The waiting time can range from 30 minutes to even 1 hour. However, they have now expanded their seating capacity, and there is also a lift available to reach the first floor.

The place is also very reasonably priced. We were a group of four friends and ordered around 7–8 items, yet the total bill was only around ₹1200.

You will find a wide variety of Maharashtrian dishes here, and they have also started serving some South Indian snacks.

Must try: Modak, Aamras, and Misal Pav
You can also try the Batata Vada.

Overall, it is a great place for pure vegetarian food and definitely worth visiting with friends and family.

featured_reviews.name: Vignesh
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best places for authentic Maharashtrian cuisine with exceptional flavors. We tried the thali, thalipeeth, vada pav, and kurma puri, and every dish was perfectly prepared—well-balanced, flavorful, and needing nothing extra. It’s easy to see why this place is already so popular in Dadar. The only drawback is the compact seating arrangement. Also, be prepared for a waiting time of around 15–30 minutes during peak hours or on busy days.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Aaswad Uphar Gruh & Mithai recently and had a proper Maharashtrian भोजन experience.
We tried a variety of items including Puri Bhaji, Seasonal Thali, Puran Poli, Lime Juice, Buttermilk, Kothimbir Vadi, and other traditional dishes. The food overall had that authentic, homely Maharashtrian taste which Aaswad is known for.
👉 Taste:
Most dishes were flavorful and well-prepared. The Puran Poli stood out – soft, perfectly sweet, and very satisfying. The Kothimbir Vadi was crispy and nicely spiced. The Seasonal Thali gave a good variety and felt wholesome.
👉 Quantity & Quality:
Portion sizes are decent, and ingredients taste fresh. It gives a proper “ghar jaisa khaana” vibe.
👉 Service & Waiting Time:
Had to wait around 40 minutes, which is quite long. The place gets very crowded, especially during peak hours.
👉 Ambience:
Simple, traditional setup. Nothing fancy, but clean and functional. Seating can feel a bit cramped during rush hours.

featured_reviews.name: Rushikesh Kale
featured_reviews.review_text: The best place to try authentic Maharashtrian food! The Misal Pav was amazing, and the Kothimbir Vadi was delicious. We also tried the Pola Usal, which was a real highlight. You must end your meal with the Piyush -it's so refreshing! Highly recommended, but be prepared to wait at least 30 minutes in the queue. It's worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja More
featured_reviews.review_text: Aaswad Uphar & Mithai Gruh at Shivaji Park is honestly one of the best places for Maharashtrian food. Their thalipith, misal pav and kothimbir vadi are always delicious and priced very reasonably. The food tastes authentic, the place is clean and hygienic, and you really get that homely Maharashtrian flavour. There’s almost always waiting outside, but trust me — the wait is totally worth it.👌👌

featured_reviews.name: sk 1
featured_reviews.review_text: Aaswad !! Heaven for Maharashtrian cusine lovers. Great experience and great food. Awesome Misal, Sabudana wada, Batata wada, Thalipeeth and more...to get a seat, we opted for a weekday and early dinner 😃

featured_reviews.name: Sarika Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Prepared for a long wait, we were pleasantly surprised to find a table for two upon arrival. Being a week day may have also impacted numbers & wait times which otherwise apparently is a lot.
After a thorough scrutiny of the menu, we ordered pithla bhakri and a chaitra thali.
Pithla bhakri plate comes with two types of bhakris, rice & jowari.
The chaitra thali actually is good for two people which we realised when it arrived. Special mention of the jackfruit bhaaji, kajuchi usal and fresh unadulterated aamras with its natural sweetness & taste. The panah was too thick & sweet for my taste. Missed taking a pic of the thali.
My friend ordered puranpoli ice-cream for dessert & relished it. Again that is a huge portion with three scoops, too much for one person. See the pic :)
Definitely worth a visit to savour Maharashtrian cuisine in an iconic old eatery.
P.S. Five minutes walk from Dadar Aqualine metro station.

featured_reviews.name: Sumit K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Aswad Restaurant is an excellent place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food in a clean, comfortable, and welcoming environment in dadar mumbai. The restaurant maintains very high standards of hygiene, which adds greatly to the overall dining experience.

The food is not only delicious but also very affordable, making it a great option for regular meals as well as for first-time visitors wanting to explore traditional Maharashtrian cuisine. Their **Maharashtrian thali** is highly recommended, offering a wholesome and satisfying combination of flavors. Special dishes like **Bhakri–Pithla** and **Thalipeeth** are prepared perfectly and taste truly homely.

One of the highlights of Aswad is their **Modak**, which is simply the best—fresh, flavorful, and a must-try for dessert lovers. The food is mild, not overly spicy or oily, making it suitable for all age groups and ideal for those who prefer healthy, home-style meals.

The service is polite, prompt, and courteous, adding to the pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. Its convenient location near **Dadar Metro Station** makes it easily accessible in mumbai.

Overall, Aswad Restaurant is a wonderful choice for hygienic, affordable, and authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food with a comforting, home-cooked feel. Highly recommended.
